blocks.instruction: Read each situation carefully and answer the questions.

items.label: (a)
items.q: Sameer said, 'I have some wood and nails at home. I can fix the benches in the park.' What did Babita and Noor offer to do for the Van Mahotsav?
items.answer: Babita offered to repair the street light next to the park (1). Noor offered to bring saplings from her plant nursery to plant along the boundary of the park (1).

answerPoints.point: Noor – bring saplings from her nursery

items.label: (b)
items.q: Look at the people who work in your school. Name two of them (other than teachers) and write how each one helps the school.
items.answer: Any two with a correct role (1 each): school bus driver – brings children safely to school; caretaker/helper – keeps the school clean; guard – keeps the school safe; librarian – looks after books; cook – prepares meals.

items.label: (c)
items.q: During the rainy season the Chinar river overflows. What problems did the people of Kanker face, and how did they solve them?
items.answer: Movement of goods and vehicles became difficult and reaching schools and hospitals was a big challenge (1). The whole community came together and built a simple, strong bridge in two days using bamboo, stones and other material (1).

answerPoints.point: Solution: community built a bamboo-and-stone bridge

items.label: (d)
items.q: Read the riddle and answer: 'I keep letters far and near, with stamps and parcels waiting here. Write a note and drop it in.' What am I? Name one more service this place gives.
items.answer: Post office (1). It also sends parcels and important documents / money orders (1).

answerPoints.point: One more service: parcels / documents / money order

items.label: (e)
items.q: Observe your locality. Name one public place there and write two ways in which people use it.
items.answer: Any public place, e.g. park, school, market, bus stop, hospital (1). Two uses, e.g. park – playing, walking, meeting others, relaxing (1 for two uses).

items.label: (a)
items.q: I am a place where you run and play, with swings and slides to enjoy your day.

items.label: (c)
items.q: I am a hut made of bamboo and hay, built by people in Assam on Uruka.

items.answer: Mason – mends walls with bricks and cement; Khetala – agriculture specialists of Sikkim; Van Mahotsav – tree planting festival, 1–7 July; Uruka – first day of Magh Bihu; Kanker – community bridge over the Chinar river. 1 mark per pair.

items.answer: Ants and bees (½ each). Also accept termites, wasps.

blocks.instruction: Answer the following questions in two or three sentences.

items.label: (i)
items.q: What is Van Mahotsav? When is it celebrated and why?
items.answer: Van Mahotsav is the Tree Planting Festival of India (1). It is celebrated every year in the rainy season from 1 July to 7 July (1). People plant trees to protect the environment and make the earth greener (1).

items.label: (ii)
items.q: Why is it important to have places like parks, schools, hospitals and bus stops in a locality?
items.answer: Everyone uses them — they are for playing, learning, treatment and travel (1). They give people a place to meet, relax and celebrate together (1). Shared experiences in these places bring people closer and build the community (1).

answerPoints.point: Used by everyone for daily needs

items.label: (iii)
items.q: How does an ant colony work like a human community?
items.answer: Every ant has a special job (1): some collect food, some look after the babies and some protect the home (1). In the same way, people in a community do different jobs and work together to make life better for everyone (1).

answerPoints.point: Each ant has a special job

items.label: (iv)
items.q: Describe the community feast after the tree plantation.
items.answer: Vegetables and cereals were brought by the villagers and food was cooked together (1). Children handed out banana leaves and volunteers served the food; everyone sat and ate together with jokes and laughter (1). After the feast the leaves were put in a pit, where they become manure (1).

answerPoints.point: Children gave leaves, everyone ate together
Leaves put in a pit to become manure

items.label: (v)
items.q: What is Uruka? How do people celebrate it?
items.answer: Uruka is the first day of Magh Bihu, celebrated on 14 January in Assam (1). People come together to build a hut of bamboo and hay called Bhela Ghar (1). The celebration ends with a big feast where they cook, eat and dance together (1).

answerPoints.point: First day of Magh Bihu, 14 Jan, Assam
Bhela Ghar of bamboo and hay

blocks.instruction: Complete the table in your answer book.

items.q: Copy and complete the table for people at work in a park. For each occupation write what they do and one material or tool they use: Mason, Gardener, Electrician, Carpenter, Painter.
items.answer: Mason – mends walls with bricks and cement – trowel; Gardener – plants and waters saplings – spade/watering can; Electrician – repairs lights and wires – screwdriver/tester; Carpenter – fixes benches – hammer, nails, saw; Painter – paints walls – brush, paint. 1 mark per row (½ for work, ½ for tool).

items.label: (i)
items.q: The river that overflows in Kanker during the rainy season.

items.label: (ii)
items.q: The date on which Uruka is celebrated.

items.label: (iii)
items.q: The state where the community practice of Khetala is followed.

items.label: (iv)

items.label: (i)
items.q: Mallika wanted to clean the park and plant trees.
items.answer: Her grandmother and her friends walk in the park every morning (1). A clean park with trees would make their walks more enjoyable and give them better air to breathe (1).

items.label: (ii)
items.q: It is important for communities to come together in times of need.
items.answer: Together people can solve big problems that one person cannot, like building the bridge in Kanker (1). Working together makes the work faster and easier and brings people closer (1).

items.label: (iii)
items.q: We should keep public places clean and safe.
items.answer: Public places are used by everyone, so they belong to all of us (1). Clean and safe places are healthy and pleasant for playing, relaxing and meeting others (1).

items.label: (i)
items.q: How did the park look after the Van Mahotsav celebration?
items.answer: It looked beautiful with newly planted saplings (1), clean paths and painted walls (1).

items.label: (ii)
items.q: Write two questions you would ask a neighbour to learn about their work.
items.answer: Any two (1 each): What do you like most about your work? What tools or things do you use? What challenges do you face?

blocks.instruction: Answer in detail (five to six sentences).

items.label: (i)
items.q: Describe how the people of Chandan's village prepared for and celebrated Van Mahotsav.
items.answer: Children, parents and villagers gathered under the banyan tree to plan (1). Sameer fixed the benches, Babita repaired the street light and Noor brought saplings (1). On the day, groups were formed for cleaning, planting, watering and cooking; Mallika made announcements (1). The park became beautiful with saplings, clean paths and painted walls (1). Everyone shared a community feast on banana leaves (1).

answerPoints.point: Repairs and saplings by Sameer, Babita, Noor
Groups for cleaning, planting, watering, cooking

items.label: (ii)
items.q:
How does helping others and working together make our community better? Write five sentences.
OR
Write five ways in which we can take care of nature and our neighbourhood.
items.answer: First option, 1 mark per sensible point: work gets done faster; big problems get solved (bridge example); people feel they belong; public places stay clean and safe; everyone learns from each other. OR option, 1 mark each for five ways: plant trees; keep the park and streets clean; do not litter; save water; put food and water for birds; say no to plastic; help neighbours.
items.markingGuide: Five sensible, correct sentences — 5; three or four — 3; one or two — 1.

items.q: Draw a colourful poster inviting people of your neighbourhood to join Van Mahotsav. Write the name of the festival, the date, and one line telling people why they should come.
items.answer: Poster shows the festival name (1), the date 1–7 July (1) and a clear inviting message with a drawing of a tree or sapling (1).
items.markingGuide: All three parts present and neat — 3; two parts — 2; one part — 1.

items.q: Your class has decided to make one thing better in your locality — cleaning, helping others or organising an event. Write the situation you would choose, the activity your group would do, and your own role in it.
items.answer: A clear situation, e.g. dirty lane / no plants in the park (1); a suitable activity, e.g. cleanliness drive / tree plantation (1); the child's own role, e.g. collecting garbage bags, watering plants, telling neighbours (1).
